scope.method: Targeted static security review (auth, session, CSRF, uploads, file serving, SQL usage)
limitations: No dependency CVE scan included in this file

passed_controls: Prepared statements broadly used for SQL inputs
CSRF tokens validated for web POST routes
Bearer API tokens are stored hashed (sha256)
Serve endpoints require auth + capability checks
Upload handlers validate MIME type and uploaded-file source
Web login rotates session id: Auth::login() calls session_regenerate_id(true) (SEC-2026-001 remediated)

findings.title: Session fixation risk: missing session ID regeneration on login
evidence: No session_regenerate_id() usage found across codebase
Remediated: Core/Auth.php login() now calls session_regenerate_id(true) when session is active; AuthController calls Auth::login() before UserSession::onLogin() on password and 2FA verify paths
findings.risk: An attacker who can set or predict a victim session ID before login may retain authenticated session access after victim logs in.
findings.recommendation: Call session_regenerate_id(true) immediately after successful login (web auth flow), and consider regenerating after 2FA verification as well.
findings.remediation_notes: Implemented in Core/Auth::login() so both direct login and post-2FA verification rotate the session id before user_sessions is written.

findings.title: Upload hardening gaps (size/content validation)
evidence: App/Controllers/StructureController.php -> handleUpload() validates MIME but no explicit max size checks
App/Controllers/GrievanceController.php -> handleStatusUpload()/uploadOneAttachmentCard() validate MIME but no explicit max size checks
findings.risk: Large uploads can increase storage/DoS risk; MIME-only controls can be bypassed by crafted files in some environments.
findings.recommendation: Enforce per-file size limits server-side, add extension allowlist consistency checks, and optionally re-encode images or use deeper file signature validation.

findings.title: Authorization model relies on broad role name checks in some paths
evidence: Core/Auth.php -> isAdmin() based on role_name string comparison
Multiple controllers gate elevated behaviors via Auth::isAdmin()
findings.risk: Role-name coupling can create fragility if roles are renamed/misconfigured; capability checks are generally safer as single source of truth.
findings.recommendation: Prefer explicit capabilities for privileged actions; keep isAdmin checks only where truly required as global bypass.

findings.title: Potential sensitive logging of auth activity metadata
evidence: App/Controllers/Api/AuthController.php logs login attempts with username
Core/Logger.php writes plain-text logs under logs/
findings.risk: User identifiers in logs are useful for audit, but may increase sensitivity of log files.
findings.recommendation: Keep strict file permissions on logs, rotate logs, and avoid adding secrets/tokens/passwords to log context.

findings.title: API token lifecycle can be strengthened
evidence: No token binding to device/user-agent/IP in validation path
findings.risk: Long-lived tokens increase impact window if token is leaked.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable shorter expiry, optional rolling refresh strategy, and token metadata controls (last_used_at/device).

findings.title: File serving endpoints could add defensive response headers
evidence: Structure and grievance serve endpoints set Content-Type and Content-Length only
findings.risk: Browser content sniffing/cache behavior may be less constrained than desired.
findings.recommendation: Add headers like X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and explicit Cache-Control based on sensitivity.

priority_actions.action: Implement session_regenerate_id(true) on login and post-2FA completion — DONE (Auth::login, 2026-04-15)
Add upload max-size and stricter file validation rules for all upload handlers
Harden token policy (expiry + metadata/rotation) and document operational standards

after_fixes: Validate new session ID issuance after login and 2FA
Attempt oversized and malformed uploads to confirm rejection
Confirm privileged actions still enforce expected capability matrix
Review logs and headers for sensitive endpoints
